faqs.question: How do I know for sure whether it is Propose Day right now?
faqs.answer: Open the calendar on your phone and read the date. If it says 8 February, it is Propose Day; if it says anything else, it is not. The date never moves, so no other check is needed.

faqs.question: Is Propose Day on 7 February or 8 February?
faqs.answer: 8 February. 7 February is Rose Day, the first of Valentine week's eight dated days, and Propose Day is the second. Mixing the two up is the most common date error around this week.

faqs.question: Does Propose Day fall on the same day of the week every year?
faqs.answer: No. The date is fixed at 8 February but the weekday shifts: Sunday in 2026, Monday in 2027, Tuesday in 2028, Thursday in 2029 and Friday in 2030, all checked with the date command on 24 September 2026. That shift is why reposted lists go stale.

faqs.question: How many days are left until Propose Day?
faqs.answer: Count forward from today to the next 8 February — that is the whole calculation, and your phone's calendar will do it. If 8 February has already passed this year, count to 8 February next year instead.

faqs.question: I missed Propose Day. Is it too late to do anything?
faqs.answer: No, and you have more company than you would expect. In the platform's Raksha Bandhan 2026 sample of 89 pages, 11.2% were built after the occasion had already passed. A late message that names the delay usually lands better than a rushed on-time one.

faqs.question: Is Propose Day an official holiday anywhere?
faqs.answer: No calendar authority sets it. Valentine week is a media and retail convention, and a search of Crossref and Europe PMC on 24 September 2026 found no peer-reviewed source documenting its day-by-day structure, so this page makes no claim about where it originated.

faqs.question: Which day of Valentine week comes before Propose Day?
faqs.answer: Rose Day, on 7 February. In 2027 that is a Sunday, and Propose Day is the Monday immediately after it. The week runs eight dated days to Valentine's Day on Sunday 14 February 2027.

faqs.question: Does proposing on Propose Day mean a marriage proposal?
faqs.answer: Usually not. In Indian usage 'propose' most often means asking someone to be your girlfriend or boyfriend, which is a different ask with different stakes from a marriage proposal. Choose the format that matches the ask rather than the name of the day.

faqs.question: I think I am confusing this with another day — how do I check?
faqs.answer: Name the occasion first, then look up its date, rather than the other way round. Rose Day is 7 February, Valentine's Day is 14 February, and National Girlfriend Day sits in a different month entirely.

faqs.question: Can I use Propose Day as a deadline even though it is months away?
faqs.answer: You can, and there is evidence that dated occasions work that way. Dai, Milkman and Riis found in Management Science in 2014 that searches for 'diet', gym visits and goal commitments all rise after a temporal landmark such as a new month, a birthday or a holiday.

faqs.question: Why do different websites show different Propose Day dates?
faqs.answer: Mostly because weekdays are copied forward from an older list while the date stays right, or because Rose Day and Propose Day get swapped. This page did not measure any search result page, so it makes no claim about which sites currently do which.

faqs.question: Is it worth making something today if it is not Propose Day?
faqs.answer: Often yes. Occasion-dated pages were only 144 of 3,894 pages, 3.7%, when the platform last measured it on 2026-09-09, which means 96.3% of what gets built here is made on an ordinary day with no occasion attached.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Is It Propose Day Today? Here Is the Answer, Any Day of the Year

Is it Propose Day today? No — unless the date on your phone reads 8 February. Propose Day is pinned to 8 February in every year, so the check is a date match and never a weekday match: in 2027 it lands on Monday 8 February, the second of the eight dated days that run from Rose Day on Sunday 7 February to Valentine's Day on Sunday 14 February.

On 364 days out of 365 that answer is "no", so the rest of this page is written for those 364. The figures under it are SubhSandesh's own, platform-wide across 21 page types and measured 2026-09-24: 5,148 personalised pages created since 2026-03-12, and 48.3% of shared pages opened on a phone (27,499 of 56,886 views). None is proposal-specific, because no proposal-page data exists here.

## What day is Propose Day, and how do you check it yourself?

Propose Day is the second day of Valentine week and falls on 8 February in every year. The date is fixed; only the weekday moves, which is the commonest reason people end up unsure.

Checked with the `date` command on this machine on 24 September 2026, 8 February is a Sunday in 2026, a Monday in 2027, a Tuesday in 2028, a Thursday in 2029 and a Friday in 2030. Rose Day 2027 is Sunday 7 February and Valentine's Day 2027 is Sunday 14 February, which makes eight dated days counted inclusively, not seven.

The practical check needs no website: open the calendar on your phone and read the date. For the full dated week rather than this one day, the companion page at the slug `propose-day-2027` sets out all eight days with weekdays, and the same question in Hindi is answered at `propose-day-kab-hai`.

## How far away is 8 February? Four distances, four different answers

Once the answer is "no", the useful question is not *when* but *how far*. Four bands cover every day of the year, and someone two days out needs close to the opposite advice from someone two hundred days out.

### 1. Today is 8 February — the answer is yes

**Where you are:** on the day itself, the second of Valentine week's eight dated days.

**Who this is for:** anyone who checked on the morning of Monday 8 February 2027 and got a yes.

**What to do today:** choose something finishable today. Platform-wide, 90.9% of started pages are published and shared (4,679 of 5,148, measured 2026-09-24), so finishing is rarely the bottleneck — deciding is. A [proposal scrapbook page](/proposal) ending in a YES button is the one format built around an actual ask.

**What not to do:** book a restaurant surprise for a working Monday evening without checking their calendar.

### 2. It is Valentine week, but not 8 February

**Where you are:** inside 7–14 February, on one of the other seven dated days.

**Who this is for:** anyone who saw a Valentine-week list and lost track of which day is which.

**What to do today:** name the day you are actually on. Rose Day is 7 February and Valentine's Day is 14 February; a proposal sent on 7 February is not early, it is on a different day with a different job.

**What not to do:** compress the week into one message. Eight dated days is a lot of occasions, and almost nobody marks all eight.

### 3. It is weeks away — roughly one to eight weeks out

**Where you are:** December or January, close enough to plan and far enough to change your mind.

**Who this is for:** someone who wants a date to aim at rather than something to send now.

**What to do today:** write down what you actually want to ask, then leave it alone. In Indian usage "propose" usually means asking someone to be your girlfriend or boyfriend rather than to marry you, and for that ask the ["I love you" page](/love-gf) — the most-viewed template on the site at 16,998 views, 29.9% of all page views, measured 2026-09-24 — is the honest fit.

**What not to do:** buy anything dated this far out. Plans made in December change by February.

### 4. It is months away — March to November

**Where you are:** the bulk of the year, and almost certainly where you are reading this.

**Who this is for:** someone who typed the question for a reason that has little to do with 8 February.

**What to do today:** treat today as its own occasion. Occasion-dated pages — every festival plus every wedding type — were 144 of 3,894 pages, 3.7%, when last measured on 2026-09-09; 96.3% of the platform is romantic and everyday pages built on ordinary days. A [shared daily streak](/streak) starts today and arrives at 8 February with a diary already written.

**What not to do:** wait for a date to give you permission.

## What changes as 8 February gets closer

The table pairs each distance band with what SubhSandesh's own festival data shows people do. Two disclosures belong here, not in a footnote: the lead-time sample is **Raksha Bandhan 2026**, a different, one-day occasion rather than Propose Day, and **n = 89** is small, so no per-template or per-region rate can be drawn from it.

| Distance to 8 February | Raksha Bandhan 2026 sample, n = 89 (measured 2026-09-09) | What it suggests | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 days — it is today | 49.4% built on the festival day itself; median lead time 0 days | Most people start and finish on the day | Pick a format that survives one sitting |
| 1 day out | 27.0% built the day before | 7 February is the real build day | Build on Rose Day, send on Propose Day |
| 2–7 days out | 5.6% two to three days ahead, 6.7% four or more | A thin band almost nobody occupies | Use it; those days are quieter |
| More than 7 days out | None of the 89 pages built more than 7 days ahead | The far band is empty in the data | Do something today instead |

The uncomfortable line is the last: 11.2% of the 89 pages were built after the occasion had passed, more than the 6.7% built four or more days ahead of it.

## Why so many people are unsure whether it is Propose Day today

Three reasons survive checking. The weekday moves every year — Sunday in 2026, Monday in 2027, Tuesday in 2028 — so a list copied from last year reads as plausible while being wrong.

Second, Valentine week is a media and retail convention with eight dated days and no authority that fixes them. A Crossref and Europe PMC search on 2026-09-24 for terms including *Valentine week India seven days commercial festival* returned nothing documenting the day-by-day structure, which is why this page does not tell you when or where Propose Day started.

Third, most people meet the date inside a forwarded message, and a forward carries no calendar. No search result page was measured for this question, so nothing here describes what any particular website prints — only that the date is 8 February and your phone settles it in two seconds.

## What the research actually supports about planning at a distance

The textbook claim is that far-off events are thought about in broad, abstract terms and near ones in concrete detail — which is exactly why you would expect advice to split by distance. That claim is under serious challenge, and saying so is more useful than quoting it.

The [Construal Level International Multilab Replication](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/wqbhd_v2), a Stage-2 Registered Report posted on 28 October 2025, ran 11,775 participants across 27 countries and regions. Its temporal-distance arm, N = 2,941, was a direct replication of Liberman and Trope's 1998 study and returned d = 0.08, 95% CI [0.003, 0.16], against an original effect of d = 0.92; the authors call the overall result a critical challenge to the theory.

Liberman and Trope [replied in April 2026](https://doi.org/10.1177/25152459261428024) that the project fell short on inattentive participants, non-native-speaker respondents and weak or confounded distance manipulations, and report a reanalysis plus a new replication that do show a temporal-distance effect. Separately, a [replication of the likelihood version](https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/gd6ej) failed twice, at N = 115 and N = 120 against originals of N = 20 and N = 34, with effect sizes declining as samples grew.

So the four bands above rest on this platform's lead-time numbers, not on that literature. What holds up better is the narrower finding that dated occasions work as starting points at all: Dai, Milkman and Riis reported in [Management Science in October 2014](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2014.1901) that searches for "diet", gym visits and commitments to goals all rise after a temporal landmark — a new week, month, year or semester, a birthday, a holiday. 8 February is one. So, usefully, is today.

## When a proposal page is the wrong thing to send today

Most of the time, and this page would be dishonest not to lead with it. If you came only to check a date and nothing is happening today, close the tab and set a reminder for 8 February; sending something to justify the visit is worse than sending nothing.

Two further cases where SubhSandesh is the wrong answer. If the person is in the same room, say it out loud — a link is a weaker medium than your own voice at arm's length. And if the ask is to be someone's girlfriend or boyfriend rather than to marry you, the marriage-proposal scrapbook is the wrong template; the "I love you" page linked above matches what you are actually asking.

There is also no page here for a reader checking a different occasion. If that is your question, the live page at the slug `is-it-national-girlfriend-day-today` answers the same shape of question for a different date.

## Sources

- [Effects of Psychological Distance on Mental Abstraction: A Registered Report of Four Tests of Construal Level Theory](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/wqbhd_v2) — Construal Level International Multilab Replication, PsyArXiv, 28 October 2025.
- [The Effect of Psychological Distance on Level of Construal: What Can Be Learned From the Failed Replication by CLIMR](https://doi.org/10.1177/25152459261428024) — Liberman and Trope, *Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science*, April 2026. Abstract only; publisher site returned HTTP 403.
- [Subjective Likelihood and the Construal Level of Future Events](https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/gd6ej) — Calderon and colleagues, a replication of Wakslak, Trope, Liberman and Alony (2006), PsyArXiv, 23 April 2020.
- [The Fresh Start Effect: Temporal Landmarks Motivate Aspirational Behavior](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2014.1901) — Dai, Milkman and Riis, *Management Science*, October 2014. Abstract only; the publisher's site returned HTTP 403.
